item: Conditional Variational Autoencoder with Adversarial Learning for End-to-End Text-to-Speech (VITS): One end-to-end model (VAE + normalising flow + HiFi-GAN decoder + stochastic duration predictor) reaches MOS 4.43 against 4.46 for recordings on LJ Speech and equals recordings on VCTK (4.38 vs 4.38), with speaker identity as a single global embedding, and it is the architecture under Piper.

[Representing and controlling style: markup, vocabularies, labels and model inputs / Model inputs] Emotion directions in speaker-embedding space (mean emotional minus neutral, α 0.4) give 86% emotion selection accuracy with similarity 0.705 vs 0.719; sarcasm only 61% (emoknob). That needs back-to-back neutral/styled pairs.

[The small student: what model runs locally / Evidence] Pocket TTS: 100M and smaller 18.2M / 6.9M / 1.9M English variants, about 6× real time on 2 CPU cores, clones from a WAV prompt and reproduces its recording quality; no quality numbers; licence not stated (pocket-tts).

[How much of Jonathan's speech is needed? / Identity saturates early] AdaSpeech: 20 sentences (about a minute) adapting the speaker embedding and conditional layer norm match full decoder fine-tuning (MOS 3.39 vs 3.35); quality drops below 10 sentences; a mismatch in recording conditions costs 0.30–0.35 MOS (adaspeech).

The Mirror to Our Soul? Comparisons of Spontaneous and Posed Vocal Expression of Emotion: Even at matched intensity, listeners rate spontaneous vocal emotion as more genuine than posed (3.45 vs 2.66 on 0–4), yet the acoustic differences are few and subtle (posed happiness has wider pitch range, posed anger more jitter), and high-intensity ...

[Evaluating a written voice / LLM judges] Shared extractor bias: when a judge extracts traits the same way the method does, the method beats the real author on the judge's score (0.542 vs 0.427), and the judge's score has no correlation with LUAR (r 0.013) (personalbench).

[Evaluating a written voice / LLM judges] Self-preference: a model recognises its own text 73.5% of the time and favours it (self-preference); content alone identifies the source model 50.7% of the time against 10% chance, so hiding the label is not enough (emnlp26-findings-1571).

WavMark: Watermarking for Audio Generation: WavMark hides 32 bits in each 1 s of 16 kHz audio with an invertible network, repeating the mark across the file. Of the 32 bits, 10 are a pattern used to find each segment and 22 are payload.

[Generating text in one person's voice: prompting, retrieval, refinement, training / 4. Training] Adapter mechanics: LoRA rank 1–4 suffices (lora); QLoRA matches 16-bit, needs adapters on all linear layers, loss on the response only, and data quality beats quantity (qlora); RoSA beats LoRA on maths and data-to-text but not instruction tuning, 1.9x slower (rosa).

LongLaMP: A Benchmark for Personalized Long-form Text Generation: For email completion, retrieving four of the sender's own past emails into a 7B model's prompt nearly doubles ROUGE-1 (0.177 → 0.349), by far the largest gain of the four long-form tasks; but the input already contains 20–30% of the target email and scoring ...

[How much of Jonathan's speech is needed? / Expression does not saturate early] 15 minutes of expressive speech alone gave only neutral speech (style score 58.1 vs neutral 56.0); with 4–7 h of voice-converted expressive data from another speaker and a final fine-tune on the real data it reached 67.7.

[Evaluating a written voice / 2. Leakage and splits] A prompt that contains the first sentence of the real message raises the same-author rate from 22% to 50% (personalbench); llms-imitate-style is not evidence because its prompts reuse paragraphs of the reference.

Unisyn Lexicon Release, version 1.3: Unisyn is an English pronunciation lexicon written once in accent-neutral "keysymbols" and turned into specific UK, US, Australian and New Zealand accents (down to town and speaker level) by perl rule scripts, with SAMPA or IPA output: the natural source for ...

[Evaluating the spoken voice / Evidence] Expression: the right test is forced-choice emotion identification plus "real or acted?" with unbiased hit rates (acting-experience-vocal-emotion); genuineness is a separate scale from intensity (spontaneous-vs-posed-vocal-emotion); a style can be recognised and still be the teacher's generic version (H3), so compare with his own take of the same style.

The Geneva Minimalistic Acoustic Parameter Set (GeMAPS) for Voice Research and Affective Computing: eGeMAPS is a fixed, documented set of 88 interpretable voice parameters (pitch in semitones, loudness, jitter, shimmer, HNR, formants, spectral balance, MFCC 1–4, voiced and pause timing) that matches 6,000-feature sets on arousal (79.7% vs 78.0% UAR) but ...

[Synthetic augmentation: how much teacher audio, and how to keep it honest / What we conclude] Filters: WER with an en-GB normaliser (looser for expressive), forced-alignment plausibility, duration and rate outliers, speaker similarity to held-out real takes on a calibrated verifier, pitch distribution per style against his, and too-high similarity to one reference (copying).

[Generating text in one person's voice: prompting, retrieval, refinement, training / 6. What we conclude] Privacy gates for any trained model: strip quotes and signatures, dedupe within threads, replace third-party names with consistent placeholders, audit with a fine-tuned/base perplexity ratio before use.

EmoV-DB (repository README): The released corpus is four English speakers (Spk-No's French data is not listed), downloadable from OpenSLR 115, with a Montreal Forced Aligner recipe that trims nonverbal sounds before and after each sentence.

[The small student: what model runs locally / What we conclude] Store what this family needs: forced-alignment durations, F0 with voicing, and energy for every take, from audio kept lossless at 24 kHz or above, without heavy denoising, with its gain recorded.

Matcha-TTS: A Fast TTS Architecture with Conditional Flow Matching: An 18.2M-parameter acoustic model trained with optimal-transport flow matching speaks well in 2 to 4 ODE steps (MOS 3.77 at 4 steps vs VITS 3.71 and FastSpeech 2 3.29, WER 2.15%) and needs only 4.8 GiB to train, the least of all systems compared; a ...

[Choosing a teacher: which voice-cloning model makes the synthetic data / Findings that cut across teachers] Licences: Apache-2.0 for Qwen3-TTS (read) and CosyVoice (unchecked); the bilibili Model Use License for IndexTTS does not say whether outputs may train another model; F5-TTS and XTTS are non-commercial (unchecked). For a personal, local model this may not matter, but it decides what can be published.
[Evaluating a written voice / 2. Leakage and splits] Random splits overstate: LaMP's best ROUGE-1 falls from 0.586 to 0.547 under a time split (lamp); Panza used a random 80/20 split (panza-arxiv).

Residual Adapters for Few-Shot Text-to-Speech Speaker Adaptation: With a frozen 89M backbone trained on 243 h from 31 professional speakers, tiny residual adapters (0.1M parameters, 0.1%) in the decoder gave the same naturalness from 1, 5 or 30 minutes of a new neutral US speaker (MOS 4.42–4.46 female, 4.46–4.51 male, Table ...

[Checking each take: transcripts, alignment, speaker and quality / Evidence] Emotion. emotion2vec reaches about 72% on acted IEMOCAP and 82% on RAVDESS but 28% UA on natural MELD (emotion2vec); a style classifier fell from 92.5% (read) to 75.7% (improvised) and 27% on another corpus (expresso).

What are neural text to speech HD voices? (Azure Speech): Azure's LLM-based HD voices come in three families (Dragon HD, Dragon HD Omni with 700+ voices and sampling knobs, and HD Flash), infer style from the text and take explicit style markers on English text, but drop most SSML control (no prosody, emphasis or break on Omni) and name no en-GB voice on this page.
[Audience, medium and time: why one person has many written voices / Evidence] Power.

[Choosing what to record next: ranking and active learning / Evidence] Active learning for TTS. Seki et al. keep the candidates the current model renders badly: 71.0% of speakers pass the quality bar vs 66.6% for quality-only and 42.6% for all data; UTMOS 2.60 vs 2.51 core-set vs 2.42 random.

Towards End-to-End Prosody Transfer for Expressive Speech Synthesis with Tacotron: A 128-D reference embedding of the target audio makes Tacotron copy a reference's rhythm and pitch closely ("say it like this"), but it transfers pitch in absolute terms and leaks speaker identity: a speaker classifier heard the reference speaker in 61% of outputs and the intended target in only 21%.

[Audience, medium and time: why one person has many written voices / What we conclude] Every sample keeps: medium, thread id, timestamp, the incoming message it answers, recipient id (an opaque id, not the name in the text), recipient count, and a relationship class (above / peer / below, close / distant), plus whether the message asks for something.

The Emotional Voices Database: Towards Controlling the Emotion Dimension in Voice Generation Systems: Actors read CMU Arctic sentences in five acted styles (neutral, amused, angry, sleepy, disgusted), one style per session, with speech-laughs, yawns and affect bursts encouraged: a few hundred sentences per style were enough for a small neutral-to-angry ...

[Data collection: what to record and keep now / 1.2 How each prompt is given] Scenario card: two lines of situation, then the sentence; "not your stage voice: imagine it and say it your way" (acting-experience-vocal-emotion).

[How much of Jonathan's speech is needed? / What we conclude] Expressive speech: aim for 3–5 minutes per target style before synthesising it (the 15–30 min total in low-resource-expressive-da over 4–5 styles), split across sessions, and plan for augmentation and a real-only final fine-tune; never expect the style from real data alone at this size.

Lina-Speech: Gated Linear Attention and Initial-State Tuning for Multi-Sample Prompting Text-To-Speech Synthesis: Instead of a few seconds of prompt audio, a recurrent (gated linear attention) TTS can absorb 45 s to 20 min of one speaker's or one style's recordings by tuning only a rank-1 initial state in under 20 s on an RTX 4090, and that raised listener-rated speaker ...

[Data collection: what to record and keep now / 1.3 Recording conditions] Lossless, at least 24 kHz (48 kHz master is fine), no denoising or loudness normalisation applied to the master, gain recorded (libritts, vocos, hifigan).

ITU-T Recommendation P.808: Subjective evaluation of speech quality with a crowdsourcing approach: P.808 moves P.800's ACR, DCR and CCR tests online: workers pass a qualification job (hearing, language, device), a training job that expires, and short rating jobs of 5–15 stimuli with a headphone check, a fixed volume, and gold and trapping questions; it ...

[How much of Jonathan's speech is needed? / Identity saturates early] FastPitch + HiFi-GAN adaptation: MOS 2.81 at 1 min, 3.21 at 5 min, 3.40 at 30 min, 3.39 at 60 min, against real recordings at 3.94; speaking rate drifts at 1 min (16.3 vs 13.1 phones/s) and the vocoder needs fine-tuning too (arxiv-2110.05798).
[Choosing what to record next: ranking and active learning / Evidence] The same idea applied to LLM scripts.

Qwen3-TTS (repository README): Only the five 12 Hz models are released (1.7B Base, CustomVoice, VoiceDesign; 0.6B Base, CustomVoice): Base clones from reference audio plus its transcript but takes no instruction, CustomVoice takes instructions but only for 9 preset voices, and fine-tuning instructions are in finetuning/.

[Evaluating the spoken voice / Evidence] Automatic metrics on expressive speech: UTMOS correlated −0.10 to −0.17 with humans, NISQA about 0, Gemini 0.12–0.17 (controllable-tts-survey); speaker similarity disagreed with SMOS (indextts2); see spoken-dataset-qa.md.
